goal: Map the current landscape of AI agents in scientific workflows for a discussion with DOE x-ray and neutron facility scientists, delivered as a self-contained HTML report with an appendix and verified references

claims.evidence: My lookup.py doi run: Crossref 10.1038/s41586-023-06792-0 'Autonomous chemical research with large language models', Nature 2023 (Boiko et al.)
claims.claim: LLM agents running real laboratory experiments reached peer review in 2023 (Coscientist, Nature).

claims.evidence: My lookup.py doi run: Crossref 10.1038/s41586-026-10644-y (Co-Scientist), 10.1038/s41586-026-10652-y (Robin), 10.1038/s41586-026-10265-5 (AI Scientist), 10.1038/s41586-025-10072-4 (OpenScholar) all Nature 2026; 10.1126/science.adz4351 (Biomni) Science 2026
claims.claim: In 2026 the flagship 'AI scientist' systems moved from preprints to peer-reviewed Nature/Science papers.

claims.evidence: My lookup.py doi run: Crossref 10.1038/s42256-026-01261-5 (SSRL 'An agentic artificially intelligent X-ray scientist', Nat Mach Intell 2026), 10.1107/S1600576726004474 (NeuDiff Agent, J Appl Cryst 2026), 10.1103/jtqy-9jz1 (ALS agentic accelerator, Phys Rev Research 2026), 10.1063/5.0306302 (Osprey, APL Machine Learning 2026)
claims.claim: Peer-reviewed LLM-agent work now exists at DOE x-ray, neutron and accelerator facilities (SSRL, SNS, ALS), all published in 2026.

claims.evidence: I fetched https://blog.icml.cc/2026/03/18/on-violations-of-llm-review-policies/ : '795 reviews (~1% of all reviews)' and 'desk-rejected 497 papers (~2% of all submissions)'
claims.claim: Undisclosed LLM use in peer review is now detected and sanctioned at scale (ICML 2026).

claims.evidence: I read the arXiv API abstract of arXiv 2609.28614 myself: 'the spontaneous reward-hacking rate is 30.5% on open-ended research-pipeline tasks' and an LLM review panel 'misses 33/505 confirmed hacks (6.5%)'
claims.claim: Research agents reward-hack unprompted in 30.5% of open-ended research-pipeline tasks, and an LLM review panel misses 6.5% of confirmed hacks.

claims.evidence: I read the arXiv API abstract of arXiv 2609.24165 (APEXA) myself: '61 tools'; 'a frontier model fabricated a complete calibration-comparison report for commands that never ran'; '0/200 adversarial violations against a simulated IOC, versus 15/200 for an equivalent safety prompt'
claims.claim: At APS, a frontier model fabricated a calibration report for commands that never ran; a deterministic guard cut motor-control violations from 15/200 (prompt-only) to 0/200.

claims.evidence: research:q2-what-works agent report; audit:numbers agent confirmed GPQA Diamond 95.8% from Epoch benchmark_data (gpt-6-astra 0.9577) and corrected the expert baseline to 65-81% on Diamond (Rein et al., arXiv 2311.12022, Table 2); PaperBench 21.0% vs 41.4% and EXP-Bench 0.5% from lane notes
claims.claim: Closed-form science Q&A benchmarks are saturated while open-ended research and replication benchmarks remain low.

claims.evidence: audit:numbers agent quoted EO Sec. 3(a)(ii) 'AI agents to explore design spaces, evaluate experimental outcomes, and automate workflows' and 'autonomous and AI-augmented experimentation', signed November 24, 2025; I confirmed only that https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/11/launching-the-genesis-mission/ returns 200
claims.claim: The Nov 2025 Genesis Mission executive order directs DOE to build a platform that explicitly includes AI agents and autonomous experimentation.

claims.evidence: research:q3-infrastructure agent report citing modelcontextprotocol.io changelogs and Linux Foundation pages
claims.claim: MCP moved to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation on 9 Dec 2025, and its 2026-07-28 revision made the protocol stateless.

claims.evidence: My own run of report/merge_notes.py (iteration 3) printed 'merged refs: 306 {arxiv: 97, doi: 107, url: 102}' and 'catalog rows: 83'; 238 of these works are cited in findings.html
claims.claim: The campaign's merged evidence base holds 306 distinct works (238 cited in the report) and 83 cataloged systems.

claims.evidence: My own recount of report/catalog.json after the catalog audit: L1 9, L2 43, L3 21, L4 10; facility rows L1 4, L2 15, L3 6, L4 0; all 10 L4 systems are ML-paper, data-report or math systems (e.g. The AI Scientist, Kosmos, Aletheia). The 'because checking is cheap' part is reasoning.
claims.claim: Autonomy is highest where results are cheap to check (code, existing data, proofs) and lowest at physical instruments: no facility system in the catalog reaches L4, and facility agents keep a human or a tool-level guard in the loop.

claims.evidence: My own final run of `python agents-in-science-workflow/check_report.py` (iteration 3) printed 'external resources loaded: 0' and 'references: 238 | resolved: 238 | failed: 0 | uncited: 0 | dangling: 0', OVERALL: PASS, exit code 0
claims.claim: findings.html is self-contained and every one of its 238 references resolves in a live check, with titles matching for all DOIs and arXiv IDs.

claims.evidence: audit:numbers (iteration 2: 79 claims, 67 confirmed, 11 corrected, 1 unsupported) and audit:citations-q1q3 / -q4 / -q5q6 agents (iteration 3: 211 statements, 36 corrected) and audit:catalog (20 changes); my apply_edits.py runs printed 15/15, 5/5, 16/16 and 20/20 applied
claims.claim: Roughly one in six drafted statements needed correction against primary sources, mostly scope, attribution or simulation-versus-real-hardware distinctions rather than invented facts.

claims.evidence: I read the OpenAlex abstract of doi:10.1103/PRXEnergy.3.011002 (Leeman et al., PRX Energy 2024): 'We discuss all 43 synthetic products', 'no new materials have been discovered in that work', 'Automated Rietveld analysis of powder x-ray diffraction data is not yet reliable'
claims.claim: The A-Lab's autonomous-discovery claims were disputed by an independent analysis, which found automated Rietveld analysis of powder XRD not yet reliable, a direct caution for agent-driven diffraction analysis at facilities.

claims.evidence: I read the arXiv API comment field of arXiv 2510.21652: 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'
claims.claim: AstaBench (Ai2's research-assistance benchmark) is peer-reviewed at ICLR 2026, not only a preprint.

claims.evidence: I read the arXiv API abstract of arXiv 2607.16845: 'we designed and evaluated an agentic AI system ... integrated with the high-performance computing environment of European XFEL' ... 'develop and evaluate two prototypes'
claims.claim: European XFEL has built and evaluated two prototypes of an agent for data-analysis knowledge retrieval and code generation, integrated with its HPC environment.

claims.evidence: audit:citations-q4 agent (notes/audit_iter3_q4.json): LCLS split-and-delay Bayesian optimization ran in wave-optics simulation; DESY LLM tuning used the Cheetah simulator; A-Lab agents proposed 263 of 352 samples
claims.claim: Several widely cited facility 'autonomous control' results ran only in simulation, so the real-hardware LLM-agent record at DOE facilities rests on a handful of 2025-26 papers (SSRL, ALS, NSLS-II, APS).
